$comment: Chain claims-sibling convention: because `chain` is an array of compact JWS strings, the X/X_claims sibling rule extends as a PARALLEL ARRAY — `chain` is the array of __JWS_DELEGATION__ placeholders and the sibling `chain_claims` is an equal-length array whose i-th object holds the decoded claims to mint for chain[i] (each entry may carry its own nested voucher/voucher_claims pair, resolved innermost-first). `chain_hash` uses __COMPUTED_CHAIN_HASH__: the minter MUST compute the RFC-AITP-0011 §5 digest-array commitment from the minted chain strings, since the value cannot be pinned before minting. The minter strips chain_claims (and every *_claims companion) before serializing any payload.
description: Multi-hop delegation happy path (3 hops, A→B→C→D, aitp/0.3 compact-JWS shape; reuses the kat-multihop-chain-001 vector as re-specified for aitp/0.3). The root hop (A→B) appears only through the grant voucher embedded in chain[0]: voucher iss=A, sub=B, grants [read_data, write_data], src_jti = B's source TCT jti. chain[0] is B's delegation JWS to C (iss=B, sub=C, aud=A, scope [read_data], fresh jti, voucher embedded verbatim). The outer token is C's delegation JWS to D (iss=C, sub=D, aud=A, scope [read_data], fresh jti, chain=[chain[0]], chain_hash, NO voucher — exactly one root of authority, RFC-AITP-0011 §1.1). A verifies the hop limit (1+2=3 <= 3), the chain_hash digest-array commitment, every hop's JWS under the key its issuer's Manifest designates (`input.issuer_manifests`: B's and C's), the voucher under A's own key, continuity (outer.iss = chain[0].sub), per-hop jti presence/uniqueness, expiry monotonicity (1711903600 <= 1711904000 <= voucher 1711905000), and transitive scope subsetting (read_data ⊆ read_data ⊆ [read_data, write_data]). All checks pass; A peer-issues a fresh TCT for D. (RFC-AITP-0011 §2-§5.) NOTE: opt-in — core implementations MUST reject any token carrying a `chain` claim with DELEGATION_MULTIHOP_NOT_SUPPORTED (see del-007). This fixture supplies no revocation snapshot, so it does not test revocation: its expected outcome assumes "not revoked" (see the conformance README, "Revocation inputs").

expected.rationale: Every hop's JWS verifies under the key resolved from its issuer's Manifest in `input.issuer_manifests` (chain[0] under B's, outer under C's; RFC-AITP-0011 §3 step 1); the voucher inside chain[0] verifies under A's own key with voucher.sub = chain[0].iss; continuity holds (outer.iss = chain[0].sub = C); per-hop jti present and unique; expiry monotonically non-increasing rooted in voucher.exp; transitive scope check passes (read_data ⊆ read_data ⊆ [read_data, write_data]); chain_hash recomputes from the digest array of the chain strings (RFC-AITP-0011 §5).
